thought
The Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a light brown leaf with irregular holes and dried-out sections. The test image is a much darker brown, more uniformly dried and curled, and doesn't show distinct spots or holes like this reference. It appears to be a much more advanced state of decay.

Next, I will view a reference image for Die_Back.

thought
The Die_Back reference image (`Mango_Leaf_166.jpg`) shows a completely dried, brown, and curled leaf. This image is very similar to the test image, both in color and the extreme curling and drying of the leaf. This seems like a strong candidate.

Next, I will view a reference image for Powdery_Mildew.

thought
The Powdery_Mildew reference image (`Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`) shows a leaf with white, powdery fungal growth on a largely green leaf surface. This is distinctly different from the completely brown and dried leaf in the test image. This rules out Powdery_Mildew as a strong candidate.

Next, I will view a reference image for Sooty_Mould.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`) shows a leaf with black, sooty patches on a green background. This is not consistent with the completely brown and dried leaf in the test image. This rules out Sooty_Mould as a strong candidate.

So far, Die_Back is the strongest candidate due to the visual similarity of the dried and curled leaf. I have viewed one image from each class. I have 12 reference image views in total and have used 4. I will now view more images for Die_Back to confirm, and then check Anthracnose again, as its description could potentially align with an advanced stage.

I will view another Die_Back reference image.

thought
The Die_Back reference image (`Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`) again shows a dried, dark brown, and curled leaf, which is very similar to the test image. This reinforces Die_Back as the most likely candidate. I have used 5 of 16 views.

I will now view the Die_Back stem reference image as the test image also showed what might be a twig. This would further support Die_Back if it matches.

thought
The Die_Back stem reference image (`Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`) shows a dried leaf with a dried twig attached, very similar to the overall appearance of the test image. This strongly supports Die_Back. I have used 6 of 16 views.

I will now view another Anthracnose reference image to see if there's any resemblance to a more advanced stage.

thought
The Anthracnose reference image (`Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`) shows a green leaf with distinct dark spots. This is still very different from the completely brown, dried, and curled leaf in the test image. Anthracnose, based on these images, does not appear to be a match. I have used 7 of 16 views.

I will view the final Anthracnose image to be sure.

thought
The Anthracnose pod reference image (`Mango_Leaf_462.jpg`) shows a partially dried and eaten leaf, with some green remaining. This is still not a strong match for the test image, which is fully dried and brown with significant curling. I have used 8 of 16 views.

Given the strong visual similarity to Die_Back reference images and the lack of strong resemblance to Anthracnose, Powdery_Mildew, or Sooty_Mould, I am confident that the disease is Die_Back. I will now use the remaining 8 views to look at Powdery_Mildew and Sooty_Mould just to be absolutely sure.

I will view the second Powdery_Mildew reference image.

thought
The Powdery_Mildew reference image (`Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`) again shows a green leaf with white, powdery growth. This continues to be very different from the test image. I have used 9 of 16 views.

I will view the final Powdery_Mildew image.

thought
The Powdery_Mildew reference image (`Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`) also shows a green leaf with powdery white patches. Powdery_Mildew is clearly not a match. I have used 10 of 16 views.

Now I will view the second Sooty_Mould reference image.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`) shows a green leaf with brown, patchy areas, consistent with superficial mould. This is not the completely dried and curled leaf of the test image. I have used 11 of 16 views.

I will view the final Sooty_Mould image.

thought
The Sooty_Mould reference image (`Mango_Leaf_288.jpg`) again shows black, sooty patches on a green or discolored green leaf, not a uniformly dried brown leaf. Sooty_Mould is clearly not a match. I have used 12 of 16 views.

I have thoroughly reviewed images for all four classes. Die_Back is the only disease that shows strong visual similarity to the test image, which depicts a completely dried, brown, and curled mango leaf, potentially with a small twig portion. The symptom description for Die_Back also aligns well: "Leaves roll upward and turn brown with a scorch-like appearance, then drop; twigs die back from tips inward."

I have 4 more views left, but I have already established a strong visual match for Die_Back and ruled out the others. I will use the remaining views to look at Die_Back images again to ensure maximum confidence.

thought
This is the same Die_Back reference image I viewed earlier (`Mango_Leaf_166.jpg`). It confirms the visual match. I have used 13 of 16 views.

I will view another Die_Back image.

thought
This is also a Die_Back reference image I viewed earlier (`Mango_Leaf_444.jpg`). It also confirms the visual match. I have used 14 of 16 views.

I will view the stem image again to ensure the potential twig in the test image is consistent with Die_Back.

thought
This is the Die_Back stem reference image (`Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`), which further confirms the visual match, especially with the dried twig-like portion in the test image. I have used 15 of 16 views.

I will use my last view to re-examine the original test image, just to make a final comparison before making the prediction.

{"prediction": "Die_Back", "confidence": 0.95, "reasoning": "The test image shows a completely dried, dark brown, and severely curled mango leaf, with a possible attached twig. Reference images for Die_Back consistently show similar characteristics: severely dried, brown, and curled leaves, often with associated twig dieback. The symptom description for Die_Back also aligns with the visual evidence, describing leaves that 'roll upward and turn brown with a scorch-like appearance, then drop; twigs die back from tips inward'. In contrast, Anthracnose showed more distinct spots and less uniform drying, Powdery_Mildew presented as white powdery growth on green leaves, and Sooty_Mould as black superficial patches on green or discolored green leaves, none of which matched the test image. Based on strong visual similarity and consistent symptom descriptions, Die_Back is the most accurate classification."}
